prompt: Read TICKET.md and src/notify.ts in this project, then decompose the ticket into the issues you would open. Consult the Planner through run_role before you answer. Then reply with ONLY a JSON object: {"issues": [{"id": "<short slug>", "title": "<one line>", "requirements": ["R1", ...], "dependsOn": ["<id of an issue that must land first>"]}], "alreadySatisfied": ["R<n>", ...]}. Every requirement of the ticket appears in exactly one issue's `requirements`, unless the code already satisfies it -- those go in `alreadySatisfied` and get no issue. Split work where it can land separately and keep it together where it cannot: an issue is a thing one person can finish and ship. Name a dependency only where one issue genuinely cannot be done before another.

source.note: Shape invented here, against this project's own `decompose_task` tool: the orchestrator is expected to take a ticket and produce linked issues, and no task measured whether it can. The traps are the ones decomposition actually fails on -- a requirement already satisfied by the code, one requirement phrased with `and` that must stay whole, two adjacent requirements that must stay apart, and one real ordering dependency among several pairs that look like one.
